ResourceHeader.ResourceName: GOES-19 EXIS/XRS Operational Level 2 1-minute Average X-ray Irradiance
ResourceHeader.Description: GOES-19 EXIS/XRS operational Level 2 1-minute average X-ray irradiance (avg1m) product in daily NetCDF-4 files. The product provides one-minute averages of corrected primary-channel and individual-detector XRS-A (0.05-0.4 nm) and XRS-B (0.1-0.8 nm) fluxes, along with uncorrected observed fluxes and estimated electron contamination contributions. It includes the number of valid samples contributing to each average, quality flags and flags for excluded samples, primary channel information, corrected XRS-B2 quadrant currents, electron-correction status and spacecraft ancillary data. This operational processing stream is distinct from the retrospectively reprocessed science-quality Level 2 product. NOAA cautions that operational Level 1b and Level 2 data, particularly during early mission periods, may contain uncorrected issues and should not be used for scientific analysis. Consult the XRS Level 2 ReadMe and User Guide for details.

Parameter.Name: XRS-A primary average flux
Parameter.Description: One-minute average solar X-ray irradiance in the XRS-A band (0.05-0.4 nm), using the XRS-A primary-channel merged signal. Electron contamination estimated using GOES SEISS/MPS-HI has been subtracted: xrsa_flux = xrsa_flux_observed - xrsa_flux_electrons. The flux is at the spacecraft and has not been normalized to 1 AU; multiply by au_factor for the equivalent irradiance at 1 AU.

Parameter.Name: XRS-A primary average flux, without electron contamination correction
Parameter.Description: One-minute average observed XRS-A (0.05-0.4 nm) irradiance from XRS-A, before subtraction of estimated electron contamination. Reported in W/m^2 at the spacecraft, not normalized to 1 AU. The associated electron-equivalent component is xrsa_flux_electrons; the electron-corrected product is xrsa_flux.

Parameter.Name: XRS-A primary electron contamination
Parameter.Description: Estimated electron contamination in the one-minute XRS-A (0.05-0.4 nm) irradiance from XRS-A, derived using GOES SEISS/MPS-HI electron measurements. This quantity is the apparent contribution to the XRS irradiance in W/m^2, not the electron particle flux. Subtract it from xrsa_flux_observed to obtain xrsa_flux; see electron_correction_flag for correction quality and significance.

Parameter.Name: Flags for xrsa_flux
Parameter.Description: Quality/status flag for the one-minute xrsa average. A value of 0 indicates good data; flag values 1, 2, and 4 indicate eclipse, bad data, and interpolated data, respectively. Flags may be combined as bit fields. Interpret combinations using NetCDF flag_masks, flag_values, and flag_meanings.

Parameter.Name: Number of averaged measurements in xrsa_flux
Parameter.Description: Number of individual measurements contributing to the one-minute xrsa_flux average; useful for assessing sample coverage within each averaging interval.

Parameter.Name: Number of averaged measurements in xrsb_flux
Parameter.Description: Number of individual measurements contributing to the one-minute xrsb_flux average; useful for assessing sample coverage within each averaging interval.

Parameter.Name: Record start time. Neglects leap seconds since 2000-01-01
Parameter.Description: Start time of each one-minute average, in seconds since 2000-01-01 12:00:00 UTC, neglecting leap seconds.

Parameter.Name: Flags on data excluded from xrsa_flux average
Parameter.Description: Bitwise union of data-quality conditions on samples excluded from the one-minute xrsa_flux average. Possible conditions include eclipse, particle spike, calibration, off-pointing, temperature and data-quality errors, invalid mode, missing data, and Level 0 error. Consult NetCDF flag_masks and flag_meanings.

Parameter.Name: 1-AU factor
Parameter.Description: Dimensionless multiplicative factor used to convert solar X-ray irradiance measured at the GOES spacecraft to equivalent irradiance at 1 AU: F_1AU = F_spacecraft × au_factor. The reported XRS flux variables are not already normalized to 1 AU. The factor varies seasonally with the Sun-spacecraft distance (typically about 0.967-1.034 near Earth orbit).

Parameter.Name: Corrected currents for XRS-B2 quad diodes
Parameter.Description: Corrected electric currents from the four quadrants of the XRS-B2 photodiode, provided in amperes (A). This is a detector-current diagnostic, not solar irradiance or electron particle flux.

Parameter.Name: Angular offset of SPP relative to the celestial north rotational pole measured counterclockwise
Parameter.Description: Angular offset of the spacecraft solar-pointing reference relative to the celestial north rotational pole, measured counterclockwise in degrees. When Level 1b roll information is unavailable, the product uses 180 degrees for normal orientation or 0 degrees for yaw-flipped orientation.

Parameter.Name: Primary XRS channel
Parameter.Description: Bit-field identifying the primary XRS detectors used in the one-minute averages. For XRS-A, bit-mask values 1, 2, and 3 indicate A1, A2, and both; for XRS-B, values 4, 8, and 12 indicate B1, B2, and both. Both detectors can contribute within an averaging interval; refer to NetCDF flag_masks and flag_meanings.

Parameter.Name: Yaw flip flag, indicating if spacecraft is inverted
Parameter.Description: Spacecraft yaw-orientation state: upright (0), neither/transition (1), or inverted (2). During a yaw flip the flag may be 1 or the fill value; consult NetCDF flag_meanings.

Parameter.Name: Flags for electron contamination correction
Parameter.Description: Bit-field status of the GOES SEISS/MPS-HI-based electron contamination correction. The electron correction is valid when its status bit indicates 0 and invalid when the invalid-status bit is set (value 1). The interpolation flag (value 2) indicates short gaps in SEISS/MPS-HI data. The decay flag (value 4) indicates the correction is smoothly turned off over approximately 2 hours when SEISS/MPS-HI data are missing and a future value is unavailable; the correction is marked invalid after 1 hour of decay. Channel-specific significance flags (values 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, and 256 for XRS-A, XRS-B, A1, A2, B1, and B2, respectively) indicate that the estimated electron contamination exceeds 50% of the observed signal. Interpret combined flags using NetCDF flag_masks, flag_values, and flag_meanings.
